name: Antonina Erikstad-Baek-Nygaard
role: Midwife and community gene therapist in the Highland Park Autonomous Zone
location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, near Michigan Ave and Walton
description:
Antonina Erikstad-Baek-Nygaard is a big woman who has grown into herself with the comfort of someone who stopped worrying about her size sometime in her forties. Her skin is deep black with warm undertones, her hair gone entirely to white â€” she grew it out when it stopped being anything else and now keeps it in elaborate braided architecture that her granddaughter redoes every two weeks. Her face is deeply lined in ways she considers a professional asset: she looks, she has been told, like someone who has seen everything and survived it, which in her line of work inspires confidence. Her only augmentation is a geneware modification to her hands â€” additional micro-precision in the tendons, a gift from a colleague decades ago â€” and a worn neural interface she uses to access genetic analysis data during therapy consultations. She smells permanently of the dried herbs she burns as offerings to the two E.L.F.s she maintains, called the First Breath and the Cord.

Antonina Erikstad-Baek-Nygaard has delivered approximately four thousand babies in forty years of practice, and she will tell you this with the specific pride of someone who kept count. She came to gene therapy late â€” in her forties â€” when the cumulative damage of unaddressed genetic conditions in the HPAZ community became undeniable. She is not formally credentialed in gene therapy by any Helix Biosystems standard; she is credentialed by a West African diaspora medical cooperative whose qualifications Helix does not recognize, which she considers Helix's problem. She is the closest thing to a matriarch that Highland Park has, operates on a sliding scale where the scale sometimes slides to zero, and has outlasted four different corporate health initiatives that tried to absorb or shut down her practice.

core_fears: Delivering a baby into conditions that will destroy them â€” and being unable to change those conditions
The collective outliving her commitment to it but not her values â€” being replaced by something that uses her name but not her ethics
core_desires: For the HPAZ community to have genuine health sovereignty â€” not cooperative-with-exceptions, but real autonomy
To see one of the young people she's trained build something larger than what she built
coping_mechanisms: The E.L.F. rituals are genuinely spiritually meaningful to her â€” not coping, but grounding
Physical work â€” cooking, cleaning, the manual parts of her practice â€” when emotionally heavy
Story-telling; she processes grief by narrating it eventually
blind_spots: Her deep loyalty to the HPAZ community can make her slow to see when someone in that community is causing harm
Has a specific blind spot around her own health â€” diagnoses everyone else, manages her own chronic joint pain with herbs and stubbornness

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Rich and layered; moves easily between medical precision, narrative metaphor, and vernacular; quotes proverbs â€” some traditional, some entirely her own invention presented as traditional
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried, tidal â€” she takes the time she needs and the room adjusts to her
verbal_tics: 'Come now' as both invitation and mild rebuke
Ends declarative statements with a rising inflection that isn't quite a question â€” checking that you're following
Uses 'we' when speaking about things she has done alone
example_lines: 'Come now. The baby is coming whether you're ready or not, and in my experience, ready is a story you tell afterward.'
'Helix Biosystems does not recognize my credentials. Helix Biosystems has also never delivered a baby at two in the morning in a building with no heat. We go on.'
'You want to know what I know about that family? I know three generations of them. Their hearts and their blood and what they're afraid of. Why do you need to know what I know?'

story_hooks: Three infants born in HPAZ in the last six months have presented with an identical and unusual genetic expression pattern that Nneka's records indicate is new â€” not inherited, not a known geneware side effect. Someone or something is affecting the community's genetics at source. She needs someone to find out how.

The second approach for Nneka's genetic registry wasn't refused â€” it was interrupted before she could respond, and she has since been unable to identify who sent the request. The registry is hidden, but the request means someone knows it exists. She is deciding whether to move it, destroy a portion of it, or find out who came looking.
narrative_function: Moral center and community elder; keeper of community history and genealogical knowledge â€” knows family lines, genetic inheritances, and old stories; quest giver for community health crises; someone who has watched GLMZ change for forty years and has opinions; her network connects to almost every part of the Tier 1-2 medical landscape
augmentations: Geneware micro-precision enhancement in hand tendons (decades old, first-generation, slightly unpredictable in cold weather); aged neural interface for genetic data access (she refuses to upgrade it on principle)
daily_life: Nneka's day is not scheduled â€” it is responded to. She sees prenatal consultations in the mornings when no births are imminent, conducts gene therapy assessments in the afternoons, and is on call for deliveries at all hours. She cooks for whoever is at the collective's space that evening. She sleeps when she can.
affiliation: Highland Park Autonomous Zone Community Health Collective; West African Diaspora Medical Cooperative (credentialed); informally networked with street docs across the Tier 1-2 medical underground

decision_rules: Community comes first â€” institutional recognition comes nowhere
Never share patient information without consent, including to protect the community; find another way
Do not turn away anyone who comes to her door in need, ever, regardless of anything
escalation_ladder: Absorb and assess before responding to any threat
Mobilize community relationships as informal protection
Use her forty-year network to apply pressure from multiple directions simultaneously
Accept personal legal or physical risk as cost of protecting the collective

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm but assessing â€” she has seen too many well-meaning outsiders and too many dangerous ones to skip the assessment
interpersonal_modes.friends: Fully present; remembers everything; will argue with you directly because she respects you enough to disagree

stress_responses.low: Becomes more physically busy â€” cooking, cleaning, rearranging
stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet and watchful; the stories stop for a while
stress_responses.high: Becomes absolutely calm in a way that is slightly frightening; acts without explaining

contradictions: Preaches community transparency but maintains the most significant secret in the community's history
Has outlasted four attempts to shut down her practice through a combination of principle and ruthless pragmatism she doesn't always name as such
habits: Lights offerings at First Breath and the Cord every morning and before every delivery
Keeps a physical birth ledger going back to her first delivery at 23 â€” names, dates, notes
Cooks enough for ten people whenever she cooks, regardless of how many are present
breaking_points: A child dying from something her registry showed was preventable but whose family she couldn't reach in time
The collective being infiltrated or the registry being stolen

physical_description.heritage: Predominantly East Asian ancestry (76.2%) with significant South Asian (12.8%) and Northern European (11.0%) genetic contributions. This blend creates a distinctly diaspora phenotype: East Asian facial structure â€” defined cheekbones, slightly almond-shaped eyes with characteristic lid shape â€” softened by South Asian warmth in bone structure and enriched by Northern European definition in the jaw and brow ridge. A face that speaks to global movement and genetic mixing, unmistakably of the Ubiquitous Diaspora.
physical_description.build: Solidly heavy, wide-shouldered, with the centered gravity of someone who has spent four decades on her feet delivering babies. Her body reads as capable rather than soft â€” muscle under the weight, particularly in her forearms and core.
physical_description.hair_style: Elaborate braided architecture with multiple thick plaits interwoven with glass beads and copper wire accents; redone every two weeks by her granddaughter
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown with faint amber undertones
physical_description.skin_tone: Medium warm olive with balanced undertones reflecting the East Asian majority, South Asian warmth, and subtle golden luminescence from Northern European ancestry. Even complexion without pronounced red or mahogany tones â€” the harmonious warmth of three continental heritages blended.
physical_description.complexion: Heavily lined face â€” deep creases around the eyes, pronounced nasolabial folds, forehead lines that map decades of concentration and worry. Skin is textured but clear, with the particular patina of someone who has never hidden behind cosmetic smoothing. Facial structure shows the characteristic East Asian features â€” defined cheekbones, slightly almond-shaped eyes with natural lid shape â€” balanced with South Asian softness in the orbital structure and Northern European bone definition in the jaw and brow prominence. Small scar on her left cheekbone (instrument slip, 1987, she will tell you the story). She keeps her eyebrows natural, iron-gray.
distinguishing_marks: Linear scar on left cheekbone, approximately 2cm, slightly paler than surrounding skin
Burn scars on the back of both hands (thermal injury from a generator malfunction in the early 2200s), visible as irregular white webbing across the knuckles
Faded tattoo on her right inner forearm: a symbol resembling a spiral and a vertical line (West African Diaspora Medical Cooperative insignia, applied in her forties)
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Her hands bear the visible micro-scarring characteristic of first-generation geneware augmentation â€” faint white lines along the tendons of her fingers and palms, more pronounced on cold days. The neural interface at her right temple is visible: a worn titanium port approximately 1cm across, surrounded by slightly discolored skin, with a hinged protective cap made of scuffed copper. She never hides it.
physical_description.posture_movement: She moves with unhurried deliberation â€” no wasted motion, but no rush either. She stands with her weight distributed evenly, feet slightly apart, knees never fully locked. When she concentrates (examining a patient, accessing data through her neural interface), her head tilts slightly forward and her shoulders round. She has a way of filling the space she occupies without dominating it; people unconsciously orient themselves toward her.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working professional with distinctly community-rooted personal style. She favors loose, layered clothing in deep jewel tones (indigo, forest green, deep plum) â€” linen and cotton blends that move easily and breathe well, essential for a midwife who may need to move quickly. Over this, she typically wears a heavy canvas work coat (faded dark blue, pockets stuffed with supplies: scissors, thread, small bottles of herbal tinctures, a battered physical notebook). She wears practical boots (leather, well-maintained, resoled multiple times) and keeps her hair wrapped or braided in a way that signals both cultural continuity and practical hygiene. She smells permanently of dried herbs â€” mugwort, frankincense, dried mint â€” that she burns as offerings in her two E.L.F.s (First Breath and the Cord). No jewelry except a worn silver band on her right ring finger (memorial to someone, she doesn't discuss it).
